Pokrovsk Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Pokrovsk, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery's founding and demolition dates are unknown. Jews likely settled in Pokrovsk (known successively as Hryshyne, Postysheve, and Krasnoarmiisk before its current name) soon after it became an important railway station in the late 19th century. Population reached 227 (3%) by 1897; a Soviet-era Jewish school opened in 1926. Most of the 1,366 Jews recorded in 1939 escaped before German occupation in October 1941, though about 50 were murdered by the Nazis in 1942. The 2001 census recorded 63 Jews in the city.
